<header>CHAPTER FORTY-EIGHT</header>

5. That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever, and remove from them their misdeeds. That is, in the sight of God, a supreme triumph. 6. And that He may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, who harbor evil thoughts about God. Upon them is the circle of evil; God has become wrathful with them, has cursed them, and has prepared Hell for them, an evil destination. 7. To God belong the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and God is ever Mighty and Wise. 8. Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, a bearer of good tidings, and a warner, 9. That you may believe in God and His Messenger, and honor him, respect him, and glorify Him morning and evening. 10. Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you pledge allegiance only to God; the hand of God is over their hands. So whoever breaks his oath breaks it only to his own detriment, and whoever fulfills what he has covenanted with God, He will grant him a great reward. 11. Those of the desert Arabs who remained behind will say to you, "Our wealth and our families kept us occupied, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Say, "Who then possesses any power for you against God, if He intends harm for you or intends benefit for you? Rather, God is ever fully aware of what you do." 12. "Rather, you assumed that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made enticing in your hearts. You harbored evil thoughts and became a ruined people." 13. And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger, We have indeed prepared for the disbelievers a blazing fire.

<summary>This page contains verses 5 through 13 of Surah Al-Fath, contrasting the eternal rewards awaiting believers with the divine punishment prepared for hypocrites and polytheists. It addresses the solemn oath of allegiance taken to the Prophet and condemns the desert Arabs who stayed behind and made hollow excuses.</summary>
<keywords>Quran, Surah Al-Fath, Chapter 48, Paradise, believers, hypocrites, polytheists, pledge of allegiance, Bay'ah, desert Arabs, Abraham Hinckelmann</keywords>
<<<END>>>

<meta>Great Compendium of the Collected Commentaries on the Analects</meta>

If spoken in terms of the relative weight between the fundamental and the incidental, conduct is fundamental. Therefore, this chapter places conduct first and cultural learning second, setting the root before the branches. If spoken in terms of the sequence of knowledge and action, cultural learning precedes conduct. Therefore, the chapter on the Four Teachings <note>Analects 7.24, where the Master taught culture, conduct, loyalty, and trustworthiness</note> places culture first and then conduct. When examining these two chapters together, one can see that cultural learning and moral conduct must advance side by side.

○ <term>Zi Xia</term> <gloss>a disciple of Confucius</gloss> said: "If someone esteems worthiness and alters their regard for physical beauty, can exhaust their strength in serving their parents, can dedicate their life in serving their ruler, and in dealings with friends speaks with trustworthiness, even if people say they have not yet studied, I will certainly say they have studied."

<term>Zi Xia</term> <gloss>Bu Shang</gloss> was a disciple of Confucius, a native of Wei. Esteeming a worthy person for their worth and changing one's heart that delights in beauty means having genuine sincerity in loving goodness. How does the Collected Commentary explain it? It says: "Seeing the worthy and changing one's demeanor, subordinating physical attraction to the love of goodness." Master Zhu said that Confucius remarked twice that he had never seen anyone who loved virtue as much as they loved beauty. The Doctrine of the Mean also takes keeping aloof from beauty as a method for revealing one's sincerity. <term>Zhi</term> <gloss>dedicate</gloss> is like <term>wei</term> <gloss>surrender</gloss>. To surrender and dedicate one's person means not treating one's self as one's own private possession. This reflects the sincerity of altering the desire for beauty. Therefore, Master Fan's explanation is the most sound.

<margin>Great Compendium of the Collected Commentaries on the Analects</margin>
<margin>Next, establishing punctuation and reading marks</margin>

<summary>This page analyzes the complementary relationship between moral conduct and cultural study, followed by Zi Xia's discourse on true learning demonstrated through filial piety, loyalty, and integrity rather than formal schooling alone.</summary>
<keywords>Zi Xia, Confucius, Bu Shang, esteeming virtue, filial piety, loyalty, moral conduct, cultural learning, Zhu Xi</keywords>
<<<END>>>

->) בשׁו̇ם טרדי בת אוני <gloss>In the name of: Ṭardi, daughter of Oni</gloss><-
(2) הרמסדר טרדי ) אאאאאא אסירי וחתימי (3) שׁידא ודיוא וסטאנא ולטאנא ולליאתא ב<unclear>ישׁאתא</unclear> (4) דמתחזיא באלליא ומתחזי בימאמי ודמיחזי טרדי בת <unclear>.....</unclear> (5) <unclear>בשׁ</unclear>ום גבריאל מיכיאל ורופיאל אמן אמן אמן אמן סאלה הלליה כפי א א א א א א <gloss>(2) Hormisdar Ṭardi. In the name of AAAAAA, bound and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit and the evil Liliths (4) who appear by night and appear by day, and who appear to Ṭardi, daughter of <unclear>.....</unclear> (5) in the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Selah, Hallelujah, according to A A A A A A.</gloss>

### Translation

Ṭardi <term>bath</term> <gloss>daughter of</gloss> Oni (2) Hormisdar Ṭardi. In the name of AAAAAA, exorcised and sealed (3) are the Demon and the Devil and the Satan and the Curse-spirit and the evil Liliths (4) which appear by night and appear by day, and appear <note>to</note> Ṭardi <term>bath</term> <gloss>daughter of</gloss> <unclear>Oni, etc.</unclear>. (5) In the name of Gabriel, Michael, and Rophiel. Amen, Amen, Amen, Amen, Hallelia, Selah. According to AAAAAA.

### Commentary

A charm against ghosts. The interest of this bowl lies in the figure decorating the center. It represents a demon with arms and legs manacled. On either side of the figures is an enclosed space, that on the figure’s right hand bearing the inscription אסורא <gloss>prohibition</gloss> <note>original: "אסורא"</note>, that on its left, רשׁא <gloss>permission</gloss> <note>original: "רשׁא"</note>, that is, prohibition and permission. In the lower part of the body on the former side is inscribed the names of the sorcerer’s client. The pictures thus graphically presents the idea that the demon has no power over the lady in question. The picture is of better quality than the inscription, which is very illiterate. The spelling is most careless.

1. The connection of the proper names is uncertain, as also the character of the names themselves. For הרמסדר <gloss>Hormisdar</gloss> <note>original: "הרמסדר"</note> I might compare the Pahlavi *Ormazdyâr*, *Justi, p. 10a*.
2. For the repeated א <gloss>aleph</gloss>, see p. 60.
3. לטאנא <gloss>curse-spirit</gloss> <note>original: "לטאנא"</note>: probably an artificial form; compare סטנא <gloss>satana</gloss> <note>original: "סטנא"</note>, טלנא <gloss>talana</gloss> <note>original: "טלנא"</note>, שׁידנא <gloss>shedana</gloss> <note>original: "שׁידנא"</note>.

The spell binds and exorcises malevolent spirits, devils, and liliths on behalf of a client named Tardi, daughter of Oni, invoking the archangels Gabriel, Michael, and Raphael.</summary>

<margin>The Chinese councillors move to make it nine years.</margin>
All the other Tartar councillors leaned toward this opinion; but the Chinese councillors pretended as if they wished to show the Dutch even greater favor, and urged that they ought to be permitted to return only once every nine years, since the great distance of the journey would otherwise put them in too much hazard. Yet here they kept a back door open that the Tartar councillors had not noticed, understanding that the Dutch would meanwhile not be allowed to trade in *Canton*. They further suggested to the Council whether Englishmen might not easily be concealed under the semblance of Dutchmen, adding that thirty years before, the English had seized salt junks in the harbor of *Heytamon* with four ships, taken the mandarin prisoner, battered down a fortress, and committed such foul deeds besides that they were from that time declared and held to be enemies of the state, and it had then also been resolved that the English should never after be admitted into *China*. Consequently, a closer trial and better assurance of the sincerity of the Dutch ought to be had before they were admitted into the empire. For besides being contrary to custom that free trade in the realm should be granted them, it could also not be gathered that this was requested in the credentials of the ambassadors, so that they suspected the ambassadors exceeded their commission. This seemed wondrously strange to the ambassadors, and it fell upon their ears like a thunderclap to hear such things, seeing that hitherto they had entertained no other thought than that the Emperor, in accordance with the tenor of the second letter of credentials previously obtained here from the viceroys of *Canton*, had fully granted the request of the Dutch regarding free trade in *Canton*, and that they had come to *Beijing* solely to thank His Majesty for it. They could well understand that Father Adam and two other Jesuits who

<margin>Who also maintain and say that the Dutch are English.</margin>

<margin>The Jesuits are also a hindrance to the ambassadors.</margin>

<column-break/>

dwelt there had squandered around three hundred taels of silver to hinder the progress of this work, and had promised even more; as well as having made the Tartars believe that the Dutch, under the cloak of trading, sought nothing else than to gain a foothold in the country first, and afterward plunder whatever they could drag away. It also reached their ears how these three Jesuits had bitterly complained that *Macau* would be utterly impoverished by this trade. Moreover, the report of the commissioner who had been in *Canton* three years ago, along with the letter of the <term>tutang</term> <gloss>viceroy or governor</gloss>, who was still in *Canton* at that time and had then been bribed with silver by the people of *Macau*, had planted such an impression in the hearts of many that they were regarded as nothing more than a band of vagabonds who had no country, supporting themselves solely through robbery and other unlawful means, especially at sea. The ambassadors could still comprehend and understand this; but that the grand chancellor and other councillors had to be bribed with money to explain and declare to the Emperor the meaning of these words, *to be permitted to go and return*, contained in the credentials of the ambassadors, which signified nothing other than *to be permitted to trade*, seemed wondrously strange to them. For they knew no better than that the thirty-five hundred taels of silver, which they had promised by promissory note to pay the Cantonian viceroys assigned to them for that purpose, had already been distributed and paid out to the imperial councillors. When they discovered that these same viceroys had deceived them in this matter, they were forced to look for other means to attain their goal. All the other Tartar councillors leaned toward this opinion; but the Chinese councillors pretended as if they wished to show the Dutch even greater favor, and urged that they ought to be permitted to return only once every nine years, since the great distance of the journey would otherwise put them in too much hazard. Yet here they kept a back door open that the Tartar councillors had not noticed, understanding that the Dutch would meanwhile not be allowed to trade in *Canton*. They further suggested to the Council whether Englishmen might not easily be concealed under the semblance of Dutchmen, adding that thirty years before, the English had seized salt junks in the harbor of *Heytamon* with four ships, taken the mandarin prisoner, battered down a fortress, and committed such foul deeds besides that they were from that time declared and held to be enemies of the state, and it had then also been resolved that the English should never after be admitted into *China*. Consequently, a closer trial and better assurance of the sincerity of the Dutch ought to be had before they were admitted into the empire. as it is said: "You shall do no work with the firstborn of your herd" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 484. Not to shear the firstborn, and the same rule applies to other consecrated animals, as it is said: "nor shear the firstborn of your flock" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 485. Not to eat leaven on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said: "You shall eat no leavened bread with it" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, which refers to the time of slaughtering the Passover offering, whose designated time is after midday. 486. Not to leave over from the festival offering of the fourteenth until the third day, as it is said: "nor shall any of the flesh remain" <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>. 487. Not to sacrifice the Passover offering on a private altar, as it is said: "You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates" <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note>. 488. The commandment of rejoicing on the pilgrimage festivals, as it is said: "and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>. 489. The commandment of pilgrimage appearance for every male three times a year. 490. That we shall not ascend to the Chosen House on a pilgrimage festival without an offering, as it is said: "and they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>.

### The Light of the Torah: These commandments mentioned in this weekly portion divide into three categories, which correspond to the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, divine service, and acts of loving-kindness. 

Torah corresponds to the injunction: "You shall not add to it, nor diminish from it" <note>Deuteronomy 13:1</note>, which demonstrates the absolute perfection of the Torah. This accords with what the philosophers stated: regarding an entity that is completely and utterly perfect, it is impossible to speak of deficiency or excess. For if it were deficient, it would not be complete, and if it could receive an addition, it would turn out not to have been complete initially. Therefore, the definition of the perfect is that which contains neither deficiency nor excess. It is acknowledged that the Torah depends upon His great Name, which is the Tetragrammaton, as in the verse: "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalms 19:8</note>, as I explained at length in my tractate <term>Shevuot</term> <gloss>Oaths</gloss>, in the chapter entitled <term>Torah Or</term> <gloss>The Light of the Torah</gloss>. 

And as the Zohar states regarding the verse: "This is My Name forever, and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: the letters <term>Yud-Heh</term> together with "My Name" equals the numerical value of three hundred and sixty-five <note>corresponding to the negative commandments</note>; the letters <term>Vav-Heh</term> together with "My memorial" equals two hundred and forty-eight <note>corresponding to the positive commandments</note>. And Scripture states: "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>, designating Him as the absolute perfect One, possessing neither reduction nor augmentation. 

Concerning this comes the warning: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, which serves as a warning against erasing the divine Name, or tearing down a stone from the Holy Temple. Behold, the letters of the divine Name constitute the house in which He, blessed be He, dwells, and so too is the Temple. As it is written: "I am the Lord, that is My Name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters serve as an enclosure for the house, while His Name, blessed be He, is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the mystical meaning of: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." 

Divine service encompasses most of the commandments mentioned in this weekly portion. The command was given for there to be an established place, fulfilled in the Chosen House <note>the Temple in Jerusalem</note>, expressed with profound reason: "to His habitation shall you seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" alludes to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the palace of the divine Name, where the divine glory unites with the beauty of His people. This is the meaning of placing His Name there, which the Targum renders as making His Shekhinah reside there. Yet around the realm of holiness the wicked walk about, namely the <term>kelipot</term> <gloss>husks or forces of impurity</gloss>. Therefore: "Take heed to yourself that you offer not your burnt-offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### Sometimes sparks of holiness scatter outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. 

This is the secret of the commandment to transport the firstborn offerings from outside the city to the Chosen House, whereupon the branch returns to its root. Concerning them Scripture writes: "there you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning that there they shall experience elevation, and not outside. Because holiness resides in the Chosen House located within the Holy Land, we were commanded, as part of turning away from evil, to destroy all the places where the nations served their gods, and to uproot and eradicate them. This was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. 

Its mystical secret alludes to the ten nations whose power is not entirely idolatrous. The matter is that the nations present in the Land of Israel under the sovereignty of the Glorious Name serve God through the severance of saplings, which constitutes literal idolatry, whereas those in foreign lands dwell under the dominion of external forces. Just as there is a severe prohibition against tearing down a single stone from holiness, conversely it is a great commandment to demolish and destroy the subverted city and never rebuild it, for its site is defiled. 

Similarly, regarding the inciter and subverter, one must uproot and eradicate him, because he derives from the defilement of the primordial serpent, who was the original inciter. The Holy One, blessed be He, immediately declared: "Cursed are you above all cattle" <note>Genesis 3:14</note>; hence the powers of the inciter are never forgiven. The commandment instructs not to love him nor listen to him, parallel to what was said to the serpent: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman" <note>Genesis 3:15</note>. A false prophet is likewise regarded as an inciter. 

Let us return to the subject: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for first-fruits, which the priests have no permission to eat until they are set down in the Chosen House. For the first-fruits, being the first, indicate great holiness, as explained elsewhere; therefore they must go to the holy place, drawing their wisdom from there as consecrated unto God, and they are consumed in Jerusalem. 

The secret of lesser holy offerings and the second tithe is that their consumption takes place in Jerusalem. This applies to grain, wine, and oil, which are the primary staples of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat lesser holy offerings until after the sprinkling of their blood, because the blood is the life-force, after which permission is granted for the physical body to derive enjoyment. 

Know that just as the divine service, which is the sacrificial offering, is an offering to the Lord, so too is the worshipper himself. For the primary service is that one offers up oneself, in the mystery of the verse: "When any man of you brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt-offering is entirely consumed by fire because it atones for the sinful thoughts of the mind, which are spiritual; it burns upon the altar all night without impediment from the serpent. The lesser holy offerings bring peace and harmony between soul and body.

### The secret of the firstborn is the secret of holy Israel, who are called the firstborn of Israel. 

God has compassion upon them and preserves them, and they are termed the sheep of My pasture. Therefore, the firstborn animal is eaten only by the priests. The mystery of eating consecrated offerings corresponds to rectifying blemishes. For Israel is holy and Israel is called <term>adam</term> <gloss>human</gloss>, initially a holy entity. Subsequently, a blemish befell him after he sinned and became clothed in garments of skin, yet he retains redemption, in the secret of: "I will give men in exchange for you" <note>Isaiah 43:4</note>. 

This was the secret of the scapegoat dispatched to Azazel: "and he shall bear upon him all their iniquities" <note>Leviticus 16:22</note>, which our Sages interpreted to mean that their sins fall upon his head. Yet we are commanded not to inflict a blemish upon consecrated animals in order to eat them, for doing so casts a blemish upon consecrated things by one's own choice. There is likewise a prohibition against labor and shearing with consecrated animals, for even the broken fragments of the tablets retained their holiness.

### The general principle: the sacrificial service is the offering, yet the inner offering is the human being himself. 

So too, his soul is offered up upon the heavenly altar after his death, where Michael acts as the High Priest. This mystery derives from the fact that man was made in the image of God. Therefore, a grave warning was issued to be exceedingly cautious during his life regarding capital cases, not putting a person to death except after thorough investigation and cross-examination. Then his execution is considered as being executed by the hands of Heaven, in the secret of: "He is the witness, He is the judge" <note>Ethics of the Fathers 4:22</note>, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is the true witness and the true judge. 

So must the <term>Sanhedrin</term> <gloss>High Rabbinic Court</gloss> be: just as they are true judges, they must possess true testimony, meaning they must thoroughly clarify the veracity of the witnesses through careful inquiry and cross-examination. Then their judgment carries the authority of heavenly judgment, and precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones.

### Because precious in the eyes of the Lord is their death, Israel being holy through their souls which cleave above after death, the commandment was issued: 

"You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead, for you are children to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1-2</note>. By contrast, laceration and shaving baldness are the customs of the nations. That behavior is fitting for them, because upon dying they go to destruction, having no portion in this world or in the World to Come. We, however, are children of the Lord; when departing from this world, which is merely a temporary dwelling, we attain an eternal dwelling above in the presence of our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to indulge in excessive mourning or engage in those practices.

### Let us return to the subject: the human worshipper is himself the offering, as stated: "When any man of you brings an offering." 

There is an additional mystical secret here: that which is lower than man can also be elevated, through the secret of <term>gilgul</term> <gloss>transmigration of souls</gloss>, as in the verse: "Man and beast You preserve, O Lord" <note>Psalms 36:7</note>. Therefore, even regarding ordinary meat eaten for pleasure, we were commanded in the laws of ritual slaughter <note>original: "shechitah"</note> and meticulous inspection for any notch on the blade. A notch renders the animal a carcass, causing a disgrace in Israel, for who knows what transmigrated soul may reside within it? 

"You shall love your neighbor as yourself" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note> implies selecting a merciful death, which is ritual slaughter performed with a flawless blade. If the beast dies of itself, the power of defilement takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it with proper care, and there is within that clean beast or bird a spark of holiness, its soul departs in purity.

### One who consumes a limb severed from a living animal is considered as consuming flesh while a transmigrated soul is present within it. 

This is the secret of: "You shall not eat the life with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the identifying signs of kosher animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the nature of the spark manifest within them, whether it derives from the side of defilement or from the side of holiness. I elaborated on this in the portion of <term>Shemini</term>. 

When Israel conducts itself in holiness, Scripture writes of them: "And they shall make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>, for they themselves embody the sanctuary. The human body reflects three divisions: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies, the heart corresponds to the Holy Place, and from the abdomen downward corresponds to the courtyard of the sanctuary, as I explained at length in the portion of <term>Terumah</term>. When a person consumes foods derived from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the altar. Concerning this our Sages stated: now a person's table atones for him, as I explained in its appropriate place.

### Regarding the commandments of the festivals and their sacrifices, I have written concerning each in its designated place. 

The command was given to rejoice on the pilgrimage festivals, to ascend on pilgrimage, and that three times a year all your males shall appear. Our Sages noted: just as one comes to see, so one comes to be seen. Therefore, if a person desires to be seen in the Holy Temple, where the divine glory resides, he must turn away from evil, do good, and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Without this, it is forbidden to appear in the divine court, for how could a wicked person wish to appear before Him, blessed be He, bringing a festival burnt-offering of appearance? When worthy, he himself becomes an offering through the sacrifice he brings. Scripture states: "three times a year shall all your males appear" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>, alluding to Isaac, who was a complete burnt-offering.

as it is said: "You shall do no work with the firstborn of your herd" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 484. Not to shear the firstborn, and the same rule applies to other consecrated animals, as it is said: "nor shear the firstborn of your flock" <note>Deuteronomy 15:19</note>. 485. Not to eat leaven on the fourteenth of Nisan after midday, as it is said: "You shall eat no leavened bread with it" <note>Deuteronomy 16:3</note>, which refers to the time of slaughtering the Passover offering, whose designated time is after midday. 486. Not to leave over from the festival offering of the fourteenth until the third day, as it is said: "nor shall any of the flesh remain" <note>Deuteronomy 16:4</note>. 487. Not to sacrifice the Passover offering on a private altar, as it is said: "You may not sacrifice the Passover offering within any of your gates" <note>Deuteronomy 16:5</note>. 488. The commandment of rejoicing on the pilgrimage festivals, as it is said: "and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 16:11</note>. 489. The commandment of pilgrimage appearance for every male three times a year. 490. That we shall not ascend to the Chosen House on a pilgrimage festival without an offering, as it is said: "and they shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>.

### The Light of the Torah: These commandments mentioned in this weekly portion divide into three categories, which correspond to the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, divine service, and acts of loving-kindness. 

Torah corresponds to the injunction: "You shall not add to it, nor diminish from it" <note>Deuteronomy 13:1</note>, which demonstrates the absolute perfection of the Torah. This accords with what the philosophers stated: regarding an entity that is completely and utterly perfect, it is impossible to speak of deficiency or excess. For if it were deficient, it would not be complete, and if it could receive an addition, it would turn out not to have been complete initially. Therefore, the definition of the perfect is that which contains neither deficiency nor excess. It is acknowledged that the Torah depends upon His great Name, which is the Tetragrammaton, as in the verse: "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalms 19:8</note>, as I explained at length in my tractate <term>Shevuot</term> <gloss>Oaths</gloss>, in the chapter entitled <term>Torah Or</term> <gloss>The Light of the Torah</gloss>. 

And as the Zohar states regarding the verse: "This is My Name forever, and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: the letters <term>Yud-Heh</term> together with "My Name" equals the numerical value of three hundred and sixty-five <note>corresponding to the negative commandments</note>; the letters <term>Vav-Heh</term> together with "My memorial" equals two hundred and forty-eight <note>corresponding to the positive commandments</note>. And Scripture states: "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>, designating Him as the absolute perfect One, possessing neither reduction nor augmentation. 

Concerning this comes the warning: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, which serves as a warning against erasing the divine Name, or tearing down a stone from the Holy Temple. Behold, the letters of the divine Name constitute the house in which He, blessed be He, dwells, and so too is the Temple. As it is written: "I am the Lord, that is My Name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters serve as an enclosure for the house, while His Name, blessed be He, is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the mystical meaning of: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." 

Divine service encompasses most of the commandments mentioned in this weekly portion. The command was given for there to be an established place, fulfilled in the Chosen House <note>the Temple in Jerusalem</note>, expressed with profound reason: "to His habitation shall you seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" alludes to the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the palace of the divine Name, where the divine glory unites with the beauty of His people. This is the meaning of placing His Name there, which the Targum renders as making His Shekhinah reside there. Yet around the realm of holiness the wicked walk about, namely the <term>kelipot</term> <gloss>husks or forces of impurity</gloss>. Therefore: "Take heed to yourself that you offer not your burnt-offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### Sometimes sparks of holiness scatter outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inward. 

This is the secret of the commandment to transport the firstborn offerings from outside the city to the Chosen House, whereupon the branch returns to its root. Concerning them Scripture writes: "there you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning that there they shall experience elevation, and not outside. Because holiness resides in the Chosen House located within the Holy Land, we were commanded, as part of turning away from evil, to destroy all the places where the nations served their gods, and to uproot and eradicate them. This was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. 

Its mystical secret alludes to the ten nations whose power is not entirely idolatrous. The matter is that the nations present in the Land of Israel under the sovereignty of the Glorious Name serve God through the severance of saplings, which constitutes literal idolatry, whereas those in foreign lands dwell under the dominion of external forces. Just as there is a severe prohibition against tearing down a single stone from holiness, conversely it is a great commandment to demolish and destroy the subverted city and never rebuild it, for its site is defiled. 

Similarly, regarding the inciter and subverter, one must uproot and eradicate him, because he derives from the defilement of the primordial serpent, who was the original inciter. The Holy One, blessed be He, immediately declared: "Cursed are you above all cattle" <note>Genesis 3:14</note>; hence the powers of the inciter are never forgiven. The commandment instructs not to love him nor listen to him, parallel to what was said to the serpent: "And I will put enmity between you and the woman" <note>Genesis 3:15</note>. A false prophet is likewise regarded as an inciter. 

Let us return to the subject: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for first-fruits, which the priests have no permission to eat until they are set down in the Chosen House. For the first-fruits, being the first, indicate great holiness, as explained elsewhere; therefore they must go to the holy place, drawing their wisdom from there as consecrated unto God, and they are consumed in Jerusalem. 

The secret of lesser holy offerings and the second tithe is that their consumption takes place in Jerusalem. This applies to grain, wine, and oil, which are the primary staples of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat lesser holy offerings until after the sprinkling of their blood, because the blood is the life-force, after which permission is granted for the physical body to derive enjoyment. 

Know that just as the divine service, which is the sacrificial offering, is an offering to the Lord, so too is the worshipper himself. For the primary service is that one offers up oneself, in the mystery of the verse: "When any man of you brings an offering" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt-offering is entirely consumed by fire because it atones for the sinful thoughts of the mind, which are spiritual; it burns upon the altar all night without impediment from the serpent. The lesser holy offerings bring peace and harmony between soul and body.

### The secret of the firstborn is the secret of holy Israel, who are called the firstborn of Israel. 

God has compassion upon them and preserves them, and they are termed the sheep of My pasture. Therefore, the firstborn animal is eaten only by the priests. The mystery of eating consecrated offerings corresponds to rectifying blemishes. For Israel is holy and Israel is called <term>adam</term> <gloss>human</gloss>, initially a holy entity. Subsequently, a blemish befell him after he sinned and became clothed in garments of skin, yet he retains redemption, in the secret of: "I will give men in exchange for you" <note>Isaiah 43:4</note>. 

This was the secret of the scapegoat dispatched to Azazel: "and he shall bear upon him all their iniquities" <note>Leviticus 16:22</note>, which our Sages interpreted to mean that their sins fall upon his head. Yet we are commanded not to inflict a blemish upon consecrated animals in order to eat them, for doing so casts a blemish upon consecrated things by one's own choice. There is likewise a prohibition against labor and shearing with consecrated animals, for even the broken fragments of the tablets retained their holiness.

### The general principle: the sacrificial service is the offering, yet the inner offering is the human being himself. 

So too, his soul is offered up upon the heavenly altar after his death, where Michael acts as the High Priest. This mystery derives from the fact that man was made in the image of God. Therefore, a grave warning was issued to be exceedingly cautious during his life regarding capital cases, not putting a person to death except after thorough investigation and cross-examination. Then his execution is considered as being executed by the hands of Heaven, in the secret of: "He is the witness, He is the judge" <note>Ethics of the Fathers 4:22</note>, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is the true witness and the true judge. 

So must the <term>Sanhedrin</term> <gloss>High Rabbinic Court</gloss> be: just as they are true judges, they must possess true testimony, meaning they must thoroughly clarify the veracity of the witnesses through careful inquiry and cross-examination. Then their judgment carries the authority of heavenly judgment, and precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones.

### Because precious in the eyes of the Lord is their death, Israel being holy through their souls which cleave above after death, the commandment was issued: 

"You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead, for you are children to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 14:1-2</note>. By contrast, laceration and shaving baldness are the customs of the nations. That behavior is fitting for them, because upon dying they go to destruction, having no portion in this world or in the World to Come. We, however, are children of the Lord; when departing from this world, which is merely a temporary dwelling, we attain an eternal dwelling above in the presence of our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to indulge in excessive mourning or engage in those practices.

### Let us return to the subject: the human worshipper is himself the offering, as stated: "When any man of you brings an offering." 

There is an additional mystical secret here: that which is lower than man can also be elevated, through the secret of <term>gilgul</term> <gloss>transmigration of souls</gloss>, as in the verse: "Man and beast You preserve, O Lord" <note>Psalms 36:7</note>. Therefore, even regarding ordinary meat eaten for pleasure, we were commanded in the laws of ritual slaughter <note>original: "shechitah"</note> and meticulous inspection for any notch on the blade. A notch renders the animal a carcass, causing a disgrace in Israel, for who knows what transmigrated soul may reside within it? 

"You shall love your neighbor as yourself" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note> implies selecting a merciful death, which is ritual slaughter performed with a flawless blade. If the beast dies of itself, the power of defilement takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it with proper care, and there is within that clean beast or bird a spark of holiness, its soul departs in purity.

### One who consumes a limb severed from a living animal is considered as consuming flesh while a transmigrated soul is present within it. 

This is the secret of: "You shall not eat the life with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the identifying signs of kosher animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the nature of the spark manifest within them, whether it derives from the side of defilement or from the side of holiness. I elaborated on this in the portion of <term>Shemini</term>. 

When Israel conducts itself in holiness, Scripture writes of them: "And they shall make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>, for they themselves embody the sanctuary. The human body reflects three divisions: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies, the heart corresponds to the Holy Place, and from the abdomen downward corresponds to the courtyard of the sanctuary, as I explained at length in the portion of <term>Terumah</term>. When a person consumes foods derived from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the altar. Concerning this our Sages stated: now a person's table atones for him, as I explained in its appropriate place.

### Regarding the commandments of the festivals and their sacrifices, I have written concerning each in its designated place. 

The command was given to rejoice on the pilgrimage festivals, to ascend on pilgrimage, and that three times a year all your males shall appear. Our Sages noted: just as one comes to see, so one comes to be seen. Therefore, if a person desires to be seen in the Holy Temple, where the divine glory resides, he must turn away from evil, do good, and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Without this, it is forbidden to appear in the divine court, for how could a wicked person wish to appear before Him, blessed be He, bringing a festival burnt-offering of appearance? When worthy, he himself becomes an offering through the sacrifice he brings. Scripture states: "three times a year shall all your males appear" <note>Deuteronomy 16:16</note>, alluding to Isaac, who was a complete burnt-offering.
